page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-128GB is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the configuration provides 32 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with one thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity totals 128 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput alongside modest single-core execution speeds. In Geekbench testing, the instance registers a single-core score of 1,697 and an upper-quartile multi-core result of 18,317, mirrored by strong outcomes in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (255.76 GB/sec), ray tracing, and image processing. The PassMark suite similarly reflects high parallel capacity, scoring 46,209.37 overall on CPU metrics, with strong performance in cryptographic operations (36,885.04) and extended instructions (57,772.07). In contrast, raw single-core stress-ng benchmarks rank in the lower decile at 788.68, reflecting the modest 2.0 GHz base clock.

Data handling benchmarks demonstrate stable mid-range memory performance, reaching 90.98 GB/sec read bandwidth and 41.03 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 2,575.03. Redis SET operations sustain 41.12 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 15.39 GB/sec. Large language model inference remains constrained by memory architecture and the absence of hardware accelerators, recording prompt ingestion speeds of 77.28 tokens per second on 7B models and 6.61 tokens per second on 70B models.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, dedicated graphics accelerators, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external block storage and network attachments for persistent data pipelines. Given its 32-core capacity and 128 GB memory footprint, the configuration delivers favorable cost efficiency for multi-threaded batch processing, compiling tasks, container clusters, and background ETL jobs where massive core counts take precedence over single-threaded clock frequencies.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-128GB is a balanced general-purpose instance featuring 32 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 128 GB of system memory. Operating on KVM virtualization, it provides 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without bundled local storage or dedicated graphics processing units. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput, including top-quartile results in Geekbench multi-core (18,317), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and cryptographic instruction sets, offset by modest single-thread execution metrics. Memory operations are consistent, achieving 90.98 GB/sec in large-block reads and 41.12 million Redis SET operations per second. Because persistent storage and public IPv4 addresses must be attached separately, the instance is primarily adapted for scale-out compute workloads, containerized orchestration nodes, parallel data transformations, and distributed batch processing.
